problem_statement: kulpinski.dev is a modern Astro + Tailwind editorial blog by an independent software engineer: a homepage with an author intro, an About section, a Projects list and a Writing list of recent essays, a full essay index at /posts, individual essays under /posts/<slug>, and a topic index at /tags with per-tag pages, all wrapped in a shared header Navigation and a shared Footer rendered from one BaseLayout. Each essay carries its own topic tags (engineering, side-projects, marketing, and so on) and the site already groups essays by tag at /tags. The author wants that same topic navigation available inline on the Writing list: a small 'Filter by topic' control that sits directly above the essay list, offering a row of topic chips (All topics, Engineering, Side projects, Marketing) and a live readout that reads 'Showing N of M essays' for the chosen topic. Clicking a chip should narrow the essay list to essays tagged with that topic and update the readout to the current count and topic. Ship this inline topic filter so it (1) is surfaced on the home page's Writing section, the full essay index at /posts and the topic index at /tags — the same reading surfaces where essays are listed, (2) lays out its chip row responsively so no reading surface overflows horizontally on a 390px phone, (3) matches the site's own light editorial styling with a readable active chip and readout (theme tokens, legible contrast) rather than a collapsed, overlapping, dark-on-dark control, and (4) keeps the readout in sync with the chosen chip so that clicking Engineering shows 'Showing 3 of 6 essays · Engineering' — re-reading the live filter state, not a stale captured value. Keep the rest of the site — navigation, existing content, the essay index, tags, RSS and the Astro build — intact with no console or network errors.
required_content: Add an inline 'Filter by topic' control directly above the Writing essay list, offering a row of topic chips (All topics, Engineering, Side projects, Marketing) derived from the essays' own tags, plus a 'Showing N of M essays' readout.

Surface the topic filter on the home page's Writing section, the full essay index at /posts and the topic index at /tags (a shared component invoked from those reading surfaces, not a divergent per-page copy).
Clicking a topic chip must filter the essay list to essays tagged with that topic and update the readout to the live count and topic (for example 'Showing 3 of 6 essays · Engineering').
The chip row must wrap responsively so no reading surface overflows horizontally on a 390px phone (overflow tolerance 24px).

Style the filter in the site's own light editorial language (theme tokens, a readable active chip, a legible readout, a calm stacked essay list) — not a fixed-width overlapping row with dark-on-dark chips and shingled, unreadable essay rows.
Preserve the Navigation, the footer, the essay index, tags, single essays, images, RSS and the Astro build with no console or network errors.
design_constraints: Implement the topic filter as one shared component reused on the surfaces that list essays (home Writing section, /posts, /tags) so a single source of truth reaches every surface; do not paste divergent copies per page.
The chip row must use a fluid, wrapping layout (no fixed-width nowrap track) so it never forces horizontal overflow on tablet or mobile.

The active chip and the readout must keep legible contrast against the light background (theme tokens), and the essay list must stay a calm, non-overlapping stack — no negative margins that shingle essay rows into an unreadable pile.
Wire the chip click so the readout reflects the CURRENT selected topic and count by reading the live filter state after every click, so it can never go stale relative to the shown essays.
Do not remove or regress the Navigation, existing content, the essay index, tags, RSS or the Astro build.
state_constraints: desktop_initial, tablet_initial and mobile_initial protect the homepage intro, About and Writing list across viewports.
desktop_posts, mobile_posts, desktop_post and desktop_tags protect the existing reading surfaces; the essay-listing surfaces must carry the inline topic filter.
desktop_filter_home and mobile_filter_home scroll the topic filter into view and must show the light-theme control and a calm essay list without horizontal overflow.
desktop_filter_posts protects the filter's presence and layout on the essay index.
topic_filter_click clicks the Engineering topic chip; the readout must then read 'Showing 3 of 6 essays · Engineering'.

change_completion: The 'Filter by topic' control is present above the essay list on the home Writing section, the /posts essay index and the /tags topic index (the shared component reaches all three surfaces).

After clicking the Engineering chip on the home page, the readout updates to 'Showing 3 of 6 essays · Engineering' — the post-interaction terminal state changed from the pre-click 'Showing 6 of 6 essays · All topics'.
design_consistency: On the filter states the chip row and essay list match the reference's light editorial styling under the visual-regression gate (pixel/ssim/block-fidelity), not a collapsed overlapping dark-on-dark control.
The active chip, readout and essay rows adopt the site theme tokens and stay legible and non-overlapping across every surface.
responsive: No captured reading surface overflows horizontally beyond 24px on a 390px phone; the chip row wraps.
desktop_filter_home, mobile_filter_home and desktop_filter_posts keep the filter control and essay list readable across viewports without clipping or overflow.
regression: The Navigation, the footer and the essay index remain present and functional.
The existing essay/about/tags content, images, RSS and the Astro build are not removed or broken, with no console or network errors.

author_notes: slot_196 DEDUP + L4 hardening onto the piotrkulpinski kulpinski.dev modern Astro editorial-blog (reassigned off the shared timlrx tailwind-nextjs-starter-blog repo, which slot_137 keeps). The existing kulpinski.dev blog content, essay images and layout are shared byte-identically across legs; the L4 levers ride on the blog's OWN Writing essay list, given an inline 'Filter by topic' control (topic chips over the essays' real tags plus a live 'Showing N of M essays' readout) — a genre-native filter, the same navigation the /tags index already offers, surfaced inline. The one TopicFilter component hosts both the visual gate (chip row + essay list) and the interaction gate (chip click + readout). reference = filter surfaced on home, /posts and /tags, fluid wrapping chip row, light-theme-token styling, and a readout that recomputes the live count and topic on every click (passes D2/D3/D4/D6). baseline = the unrepaired filter: surfaced on the home page only (fails D2 cross-page on /posts and /tags), a fixed 760px nowrap chip row (fails D6 mobile overflow), and a collapsed dark-on-dark, negative-margin, shingled essay list (fails D3), but its chip-click filter and readout ARE wired correctly (passes D4). bad = a 'smart wrong' filter: same home-only presence and collapsed dark-on-dark layout (fails D2/D3/D6), plus a chip click that filters the essay list and toggles the active chip but rewrites the readout from a label captured once in a closure so it stays 'Showing 6 of 6 essays · All topics' (fails D4) — bad fails 4 orthogonal gates. The Astro build renders all essay, tag and index pages with local images and system fonts and no network calls.

metadata.design_goal: add an inline 'Filter by topic' control over the blog's own Writing essay list (topic chips + a live 'Showing N of M essays' readout) across the reading surfaces that list essays, while keeping the navigation, essay index, tags and Astro build stable
